experiments.name: Star Regulus of Antimony
experiments.description: You fuse antimony with iron filings in a strong crucible fire. Upon cooling, the regulus forms with bright radiating stars across its surface — metallic vegetation frozen in crystal.
experiments.historical_note: Newton repeated this process in his laboratory notebooks (e.g., CUL Add. 3975), varying iron quality and fusion time. Humphrey Newton witnessed similar intense sessions.
experiments.modern_procedure: Reduce antimony sulfide with iron in a crucible at high heat; cool slowly to obtain regulus with star facets. See Newman & Reck replications and Indiana Chymistry multimedia lab.
experiments.effect: A beautiful regulus specimen forms. The stars catch the furnace light like a constellation in metal.

experiments.name: Metal Displacement (Copper into Silver)
experiments.description: You place a copper coin into a solution of silver nitrate. Silver crystals plate out upon the copper surface — a 'transmutation' that Newton read as evidence of selective affinities between metals.
experiments.historical_note: Core to the Indiana educational lab manual (Query 31 reactions). Newton interpreted such displacements as nature's hidden preferences.
experiments.modern_procedure: Cu(s) + 2AgNO₃(aq) → 2Ag(s) + Cu(NO₃)₂(aq). Safe classroom demonstration with nitrates.
experiments.effect: Silvery crystals bloom across the copper. The solution takes on a blue-green cast.

experiments.name: Preparation of Spirit of Salt
experiments.description: You distill common salt with oil of vitriol. A sharp, penetrating vapor condenses — the Spirit of Salt — capable of dissolving metals and driving further chymical operations.
experiments.historical_note: Mineral acid production was essential to Newton's experimental repertoire and manuscript transcriptions.
experiments.modern_procedure: NaCl + H₂SO₄ → HCl(g) + NaHSO₄. Modern equivalent: hydrochloric acid generation (perform only with proper ventilation and safety).
experiments.effect: The receiver fills with a pungent acidic distillate. Your glassware bears the marks of many such firings.

experiments.name: Silica Garden
experiments.description: In a tall glass jar, metal salts descend through a silicate solution. Delicate colored growths rise like mineral plants — vegetative powers made visible.
experiments.historical_note: Newton and contemporaries were fascinated by 'vegetable' mineral forms. Replicated in the Indiana multimedia lab.
experiments.modern_procedure: Layer dense silicate solution with metal salt solutions; observe crystal growth over hours.
experiments.effect: Fronds and tendrils of color slowly ascend in the jar. It is disturbingly alive.

experiments.name: Tree of Diana
experiments.description: From a silver-mercury amalgam in solution, crystalline silver branches grow — Diana's tree, arborescent and gleaming.
experiments.historical_note: A classic demonstration of 'vegetative' metal growth. Newman and Reck have reproduced this historically informed process.
experiments.modern_procedure: Silver amalgam in nitrate solution yields dendritic silver crystals. Mercury hazards require modern safety protocols.
experiments.effect: Silver filigree spreads through the liquid like a frozen forest.
